grammar_focus: Present simple vs present continuous; state verbs
goals: popsat povahu člověka pomocí přesných přídavných jmen
jistě rozlišovat present simple a present continuous včetně stavových sloves
vést small talk s neznámým člověkem a ptát se na jeho práci, zájmy a aktuální projekty

vocab_core.ex: She's very outgoing and makes friends easily.
He was too shy to speak to her.
Tom is reliable – he never forgets a promise.
My dad is easy-going; nothing makes him angry.
She's hard-working and often stays late.
I feel lazy on Sunday mornings.
It was very generous of you to pay for dinner.
Don't be mean – share your chocolate!
To be honest, I didn't like the film.
He's ambitious and wants to run his own company.
You need to be patient with small children.
She felt confident before the interview.
He's sensitive to other people's feelings.
My grandma is too stubborn to ask for help.
Stop being so bossy – I can decide myself!
She's always cheerful, even on Mondays.
Teenagers can be quite moody.
How thoughtful of you to bring flowers!
It's selfish to think only about yourself.
My neighbour is very talkative.
I'm not very sociable – I prefer small groups.
She's very organised and plans everything.
Stay calm – everything will be fine.

blocks.label: 1A Warm-up
blocks.instr: Discuss the questions with your partner.
items: How would your best friend describe you in three words?
Which personality traits do you value most in a colleague? And in a friend?
Do you take after your mother or your father? In what way?
Are you more of an introvert or an extrovert? Does it depend on the situation?
Which quality would you like to have more of? Why?

blocks.label: 1B Core vocabulary
blocks.instr: Read the words. Tick (✓) the ones that describe you and put a cross (✗) next to the ones that definitely don't.

blocks.label: 1C Extension
blocks.instr: These compound adjectives and phrases make your descriptions more natural.

blocks.label: 1D Match
blocks.instr: Match the people (1–8) with the adjectives (a–h).
left: She always does what she promises.
He never gives money to anyone.
She tells everyone what to do.
He changes his mind about nothing – ever.
She's happy and smiling most of the time.
He talks a lot, even to strangers on the bus.
She always remembers your birthday and asks how you are.
He forgets where he put his phone every day.

blocks.label: 1E Describe someone
blocks.instr: Think of a person you know well (a family member, a friend, a colleague). Describe them to your partner using at least three adjectives from 1B–1C. Give an example for each one: My brother is very generous – last year he paid for our holiday. Your partner asks two follow-up questions.

blocks.label: Grammar review: present simple vs present continuous
blocks.html:
Present simplePresent continuous
zvyky, opakované děje
I usually get up at six.		děj probíhající právě teď
Shh, the baby is sleeping.
fakta, obecné pravdy
Water boils at 100 °C.		dočasná situace „v těchto dnech“
I'm working from home this week.
trvalé stavy
She lives in Brno.		měnící se a vyvíjející se situace
Prices are going up.
signální slova: always, usually, often, every day, neversignální slova: now, at the moment, today, this week, currently, Look! Listen!

Stavová slovesa (state verbs) se v průběhovém čase obvykle nepoužívají: know, understand, believe, think (= mít názor), like, love, hate, prefer, want, need, mean, seem, belong, own, remember.
✗ I'm knowing him. → ✓ I know him.

Slovesa se dvěma významy: I think it's a good idea (názor) × I'm thinking about my holiday (přemýšlím); She has two cats (vlastní) × She's having lunch (jí); He is rude (povaha) × He's being rude (právě teď se tak chová).

always + průběhový čas = něco nás opakovaně rozčiluje: He's always leaving his socks on the floor!

items.q: I (work / 'm working) from home this week because they're repairing our office.
My brother (doesn't like / isn't liking) big parties.
What (do you think / are you thinking) about the new manager?
She (has / is having) two older sisters.
We (have / are having) dinner at the moment – can I call you back?
He's usually very polite, but today he (is / is being) really rude.

blocks.label: 2B Complete
blocks.instr: Complete the sentences with the correct form of the verbs in brackets.

items.q: Petra ______ (live) in Brno, but this month she ______ (stay) with her parents in Prague.
More and more people ______ (work) from home these days.
My sister ______ (always borrow) my clothes without asking! It's so annoying.

blocks.label: 2C Reading
blocks.instr: Read the blog post and decide if the sentences are true (T) or false (F).
blocks.title: Living with Jake
paras: When I moved into my new flat in September, I was a bit nervous. I didn't know anything about my flatmate, Jake, except that he works as a nurse. Two months later, I can honestly say he's one of the most easy-going people I know.

Jake works long shifts at the hospital, so our routines are very different. He usually gets up at five and leaves before I wake up. On his days off, he loves cooking, and he always makes enough for both of us. He's incredibly generous – last week he even bought me a plant for my room because he thought it looked empty.

That doesn't mean he's perfect. He's quite absent-minded and often forgets his keys, so I sometimes have to open the door for him at midnight. He's also a bit stubborn about music: he believes that jazz is the only real music, and nothing I say changes his mind.

At the moment, Jake is studying for an important exam because he wants to become a specialist nurse. He's spending most evenings in his room with his books, so the flat is much quieter than usual. I'm trying to be thoughtful and I'm keeping the TV down.
Is he the perfect flatmate? Probably not. But he's honest and reliable, and he makes me laugh – and that's more than enough for me.

tf.q: The writer knew Jake well before moving in.
Jake usually gets up earlier than the writer.
Jake sometimes needs help to get into the flat.
Jake is open-minded about different kinds of music.
These days the flat is noisier than usual.

open.q: Find three examples of the present continuous in the text. Why is it used there?
open.a: is studying, is spending, 'm trying, 'm keeping – dočasná situace v současném období (at the moment, these days).

open.q: Which four adjectives from 1B–1C describe Jake? Would you like him as a flatmate?
open.a: easy-going, generous, absent-minded, stubborn, honest, reliable – vlastní odpověď.

blocks.label: 2D Listening
blocks.instr: Listen to Anna and Tom at a party (track L01). Answer the questions. If you don't have the audio, one of you reads the transcript from the key.

options: They work in the same company.

items.q: How long have Anna and Kate known each other?

items.a: She's an English teacher (at a secondary school).

items.q: Why isn't she working as a teacher this year?
items.a: She's doing a course in educational psychology.

items.q: What does she do in the afternoons?
items.a: She works part-time in a bookshop.
She goes swimming every Saturday morning.

items.q: When and where is Tom's concert?
items.a: Next Friday at the Blue Lion.

blocks.label: 2E Vocabulary: opposites
blocks.instr: Make the opposites using un-, in-, im-, ir- or dis-. Then complete the sentences below with four of the new words.

sentences.q: He's 35 but he still behaves like a teenager. He's so ______.
Don't ask Mark to help you move – he's ______ and probably won't come.
She never knows where her documents are. She's very ______.
Leaving a small child alone at home is ______.

blocks.label: 3A Find the mistake
blocks.instr: Each sentence has one mistake. Correct it.

items.q: I'm not knowing the answer to this question.
items.a: I don't know the answer to this question.

items.q: She is wanting a new phone for her birthday.
items.a: She wants a new phone for her birthday.

items.q: How often are you going to the gym?
items.a: How often do you go to the gym?

items.q: My uncle work in a bank in Ostrava.
items.a: My uncle works in a bank in Ostrava.

items.q: Listen! Somebody sings in the garden.
items.a: Listen! Somebody is singing in the garden.

items.q: My parents are owning a small cottage by a lake.
items.a: My parents own a small cottage by a lake.

items.q: I am usually drinking coffee in the morning.
items.a: I usually drink coffee in the morning.

items.q: This bag is belonging to my sister.
items.a: This bag belongs to my sister.

blocks.label: 3B Two truths and a lie
blocks.instr: Write three sentences about yourself: one about your routine (present simple), one about something you're doing these days (present continuous) and one with a state verb (like, prefer, believe, own…). One of them is a lie! Read them to your partner. Your partner asks up to five questions and then guesses the lie.

blocks.label: 3C Role-play: small talk at a party
blocks.instr: You are at a friend's birthday party and you don't know each other. Use your role card. Introduce yourselves and find at least two things in common and two differences. Use the phrases in the box.

cards.text: You're an IT specialist and you work for a bank. You live in a flat with your cat, Mia. At the moment you're learning to cook Thai food – it's going badly! You go running three times a week. You're quite shy at first but very talkative once you know people. You know the host from a running club.

You're an architect. You love old buildings, and these days you're renovating an old farmhouse in the country. You go hiking almost every weekend. You hate cooking and usually eat out. You're outgoing and curious. You know the host because you were at school together.

phrases: Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm …
What are you working on at the moment?
What do you do in your free time?
Me too! / Me neither. / Oh, I'm the opposite.
It was nice talking to you.

blocks.label: 3D Report back
blocks.instr: Tell your partner what you found out about their character in 3C, using adjectives from 1B–1C: You seem quite outgoing and curious, and you're obviously hard-working because… Does your partner agree?

blocks.label: 3E Writing (homework)
blocks.instr: Write a short profile (100–120 words) of a person who is important to you. Describe their personality, their typical routine and what they're doing in their life at the moment. Use at least five adjectives from this lesson and both present tenses.

blocks.label: 4A Memorise
blocks.instr: Learn the words below (the app will help you practise them every day). In pairs: one of you covers the English column, the other reads the Czech meaning. Swap after 10 words.

lines.text: Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Tom.
Hi Tom, I'm Anna. Nice to meet you. So, how do you know Kate?
We work for the same company. I'm in marketing and she's in sales. What about you?
We went to university together. We've known each other for years.
Oh, nice. And what do you do, Anna?
I'm a teacher. I teach English at a secondary school. But I'm not teaching this year. I'm doing a course in educational psychology, so I'm a student again.
Wow. How are you finding it?
It's hard work, but I love it. I usually study in the library in the mornings, and in the afternoons I work part-time in a bookshop.
That sounds busy. Do you have any free time at all?
Not much! But I go swimming every Saturday morning. It helps me relax. What about you? What do you do when you're not working?
I play the guitar in a band. We're not very good, but we're having a lot of fun. Actually, we're playing a small concert next Friday at the Blue Lion.
Really? What kind of music do you play?
Mostly rock. Some old classics, too. You should come! Kate's coming as well.
Maybe I will. I really need a break from my books!
